\subsubsection{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:layer-specific-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand how structure varies per layer before aggregating the network.


\paragraph{Compute Per\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Density}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:compute-per-layer-density}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Density compares observed edges \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}} to the maximum possible edges among \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} nodes in one layer.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes and edges in this layer}
    \PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Density = actual edges / possible edges}
    \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} undirected}
    \PYG{n}{density} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layer }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: density = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For directed layers, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_edges = n * (n \sphinxhyphen{} 1)}} instead (ordered pairs).


\paragraph{Compare Layers}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:compare-layers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the DSL for efficient comparison:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: avg degree = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example output (values depend on your data):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
layer1: avg degree = 3.45
layer2: avg degree = 2.87
layer3: avg degree = 4.12
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Level Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:node-level-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Once you know layer\sphinxhyphen{}level trends, drill down to node importance and activity.


\paragraph{Node Activity (Layer Count)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:node-activity-layer-count}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
How many layers does each node participate in? \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} counts unique layers where the node appears.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes present in multiple layers}
\PYG{n}{active\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{active\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example output:}

     node  layer\PYGZus{}count
0   Alice           3
1     Bob           3
2   Carol           2
3    Dave           1
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Degree Centrality}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:degree-centrality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute degree for all nodes and sort in descending order:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 10 by degree:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Betweenness Centrality}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:betweenness-centrality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find nodes that bridge different parts of the network (higher values indicate more shortest paths go through the node):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 10 by betweenness:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:multilayer-specific-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use these measures when the interaction between layers matters, not just within\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure.


\paragraph{Node Versatility}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:node-versatility}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Versatility measures how evenly a node distributes its connections across layers; higher values mean more balanced participation across layers.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{calculate\PYGZus{}versatility}

\PYG{n}{versatility\PYGZus{}scores} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calculate\PYGZus{}versatility}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sort by versatility}
\PYG{n}{sorted\PYGZus{}scores} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sorted}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{versatility\PYGZus{}scores}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 5 most versatile nodes:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{score} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{sorted\PYGZus{}scores}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{score}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Edge Overlap Between Layers}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:edge-overlap-between-layers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
How many connections exist in multiple layers?

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{How to Run Community Detection on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:how-to-run-community-detection-on-multilayer-networks}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} This guide demonstrates how to apply community detection algorithms to multilayer networks and interpret their results. Community detection identifies \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesoscale structure}—groups of nodes that are more densely connected internally than to the rest of the network. In multilayer networks, communities can exist within single layers, span multiple layers, or emerge from inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling patterns. This analysis is essential for understanding functional modules, organizational structure, and hierarchical clustering in complex systems.

\subsubsection{Quick Start: Louvain Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:quick-start-louvain-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Louvain?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Louvain algorithm (Blondel et al., 2008) is a fast, greedy method that optimizes \sphinxstyleemphasis{modularity}, defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left[ A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m} \right] \delta(c_i, c_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(A_{ij}\) is the adjacency matrix, \(k_i\) is node degree, \(m\) is total edges, and \(\delta(c_i, c_j)=1\) if nodes \(i,j\) are in the same community. Higher \(Q\) indicates stronger community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{How it works:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize: each node starts in its own community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node, compute \(\Delta Q\) from moving to each neighbor’s community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Move the node to the community with maximum positive \(\Delta Q\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate: collapse communities into super\sphinxhyphen{}nodes and repeat

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stop when no further improvement is possible

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time complexity:} \(O(n \log n)\) for sparse networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific: Multilayer Louvain}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:multilayer-specific-multilayer-louvain}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What makes multilayer community detection different?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Standard Louvain treats a multilayer network as a single flattened graph, losing layer identity. \sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Louvain} (Mucha et al., 2010) optimizes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{multilayer modularity}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q_{\text{multi}} = \frac{1}{2\mu} \sum_{ij\alpha\beta} \left[ \left(A^\alpha_{ij} - \gamma^\alpha \frac{k_i^\alpha k_j^\alpha}{2m_\alpha}\right)\delta_{\alpha\beta} + \delta_{ij}\omega_{\alpha\beta} \right] \delta(g_{i\alpha}, g_{j\beta})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A^\alpha_{ij}\): adjacency in layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(k_i^\alpha\): degree (or strength) of node \(i\) in layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(m_\alpha\): total edge weight in layer \(\alpha\) (\(2m_\alpha = \sum_{ij} A_{ij}^\alpha\))

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma^\alpha\): resolution parameter for layer \(\alpha\) (default 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\): inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (default 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta_{ij}=1\) if \(i=j\) (inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges connect same node across layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta_{\alpha\beta}=1\) if \(\alpha=\beta\) (restricts intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer term)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta(g_{i\alpha}, g_{j\beta})=1\) if node \(i\) in layer \(\alpha\) and node \(j\) in layer \(\beta\) are in the same community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\mu\): total weight in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}network (\(2\mu = \sum_\alpha 2 m_\alpha + \sum_{\alpha\neq\beta}\omega_{\alpha\beta}\))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} The coupling term \(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\) controls whether communities span layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω = 0:} Layers are independent \(\rightarrow\) separate communities per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω \(\rightarrow\) \(\infty\):} Strong coupling \(\rightarrow\) communities span all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{0 \textless{} ω \textless{} \(\infty\):} Partial coupling \(\rightarrow\) communities can span some layers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Infomap Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:infomap-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Infomap?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infomap (Rosvall \& Bergstrom, 2008) uses information theory to find communities by minimizing the \sphinxstyleemphasis{map equation}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}L(M) = q_\curvearrowright H(Q) + \sum_{i=1}^m p_{\circlearrowright}^i H(P^i)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(q_\curvearrowright\): probability of switching between modules (inter\sphinxhyphen{}module flow)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(H(Q)\): entropy of module codebook

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(p_{\circlearrowright}^i\): probability of staying within module \(i\) (intra\sphinxhyphen{}module flow)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(H(P^i)\): entropy of nodes within module \(i\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} Infomap simulates a random walker and finds communities that compress the \sphinxstyleemphasis{description length} of the walker’s trajectory. Communities are regions where the walker gets “trapped” for extended periods.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros/cons vs. Louvain:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros:} Often finds better communities for flow\sphinxhyphen{}based systems (e.g., citation networks, web graphs)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cons:} Requires external binary (not pure Python), slower than Louvain, harder to interpret parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Installation:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infomap requires the standalone binary from \sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/}:

unzip\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap.zip
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap
make
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cp\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/local/bin/infomap

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or install Python wrapper (alternative)}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }infomap
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}

    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{o+ow}{not} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exists}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Falling back to Louvain...}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use Louvain as fallback}
    \PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
    \PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex mode:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex=True}}, Infomap treats layers as separate networks but allows random walkers to switch layers (implicitly modeling inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling). This is different from Louvain’s explicit \(\omega\) parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comparison workflow:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run both algorithms}
\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{binary}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to aligned label vectors}
\PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}labels} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}labels} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute similarity}
\PYG{n}{ari} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{adjusted\PYGZus{}rand\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{nmi} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{normalized\PYGZus{}mutual\PYGZus{}info\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Agreement between Louvain and Infomap:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  ARI: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{ari}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  (1.0 = perfect agreement)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  NMI: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{nmi}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  (1.0 = perfect agreement)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When to use Infomap:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Citation/web networks with clear flow patterns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Networks where you care about information diffusion

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When Louvain gives unsatisfying results (try both and compare)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When you have the binary installed (otherwise, stick with Louvain)

\subsubsection{Label Propagation}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:label-propagation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Label Propagation?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Label propagation (Raghavan et al., 2007) is an extremely fast, near\sphinxhyphen{}linear time algorithm that works by iteratively assigning each node to the most common community among its neighbors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Algorithm:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize: each node gets a unique label (community ID)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{For t=1 to T iterations:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\alph}{enumii}{enumiii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomize node order

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node \(i\):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Count neighbor labels: \(n_c = |\{j \in N(i) : c_j = c\}|\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assign \(c_i = \arg\max_c n_c\) (ties broken randomly)

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stop when labels stabilize or max iterations reached

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time complexity:} \(O(m)\) per iteration (linear in edges)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros/cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros:} Very fast, scales to millions of nodes, no parameters to tune

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cons:} Non\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic (order\sphinxhyphen{}dependent), lower quality than Louvain/Infomap, may not converge

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Implementation note:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex uses NetworkX’s label propagation for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n+nn}{networkx} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{asyn\PYGZus{}lpa\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{collections} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{defaultdict}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to NetworkX (flattened single\PYGZhy{}layer graph)}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run label propagation}
\PYG{n}{communities\PYGZus{}list} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{asyn\PYGZus{}lpa\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to dict format: node \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} community\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{enumerate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

        \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze results}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{collections} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Counter}
\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Counter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Number of communities: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Largest community: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average size: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.1f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run multiple times to check stability}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Stability check (5 runs with same seed):}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxstylestrong{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}aware label propagation (custom implementation):}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For multilayer networks, you can implement layer\sphinxhyphen{}aware label propagation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n+nn}{random}

\subsubsection{Query Communities with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:query-communities-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) to query and analyze community\sphinxhyphen{}detected networks efficiently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL provides a declarative, SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like interface for querying multilayer networks. After detecting communities, you can use DSL queries to filter nodes by community membership, compute community\sphinxhyphen{}level statistics, and extract subnetworks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection results (e.g., from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain\_communities()}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Familiarity with DSL basics (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}}}} for full tutorial)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{DSL Basics for Communities}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:dsl-basics-for-communities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String Syntax \sphinxhyphen{} SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like queries:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network and detect communities}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{py3plex/datasets/\PYGZus{}data/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Attach community labels as node attributes}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} DSL Query: Find nodes in community 0}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE community=0}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{nodes\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}comm0} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in community 0: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}comm0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes\PYGZus{}in\PYGZus{}comm0}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{Complex DSL Workflows}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: betweenness=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{betw}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.6f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{, connects }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Compare Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:compare-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different algorithms optimize different objective functions and may produce different community structures. \sphinxstylestrong{Comparing multiple algorithms} helps validate findings and understand algorithm\sphinxhyphen{}specific biases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Metrics for comparing partitions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)}: Measures similarity adjusted for chance
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}, where 1 = perfect agreement, 0 = random

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjusted for cluster size imbalance

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Normalized Mutual Information (NMI)}: Information\sphinxhyphen{}theoretic similarity
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}0, 1{]}, where 1 = perfect agreement

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Symmetric, handles different number of communities well

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Variation of Information (VI)}: Distance metric (lower = more similar)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}0, \(\infty\){]}, where 0 = identical partitions

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Quality Metrics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:quality-metrics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why quality metrics matter:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quality metrics help you:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compare algorithms} objectively

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tune parameters} (e.g., choosing optimal \(\omega\) in multilayer Louvain)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validate results} (high Q suggests real structure, not random fluctuations)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Detect overfitting} (too many tiny communities = over\sphinxhyphen{}segmentation)

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Compute Modularity}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:compute-modularity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer modularity:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For flattened networks, use the Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan modularity:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left[ A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m} \right] \delta(c_i, c_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}louvain} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{modularity}
\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n+nn}{networkx} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to NetworkX for modularity calculation}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Calculate modularity}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Modularity Q: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Interpretation}

\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.4}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Strong community structure}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Multilayer modularity Q: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{Q\PYGZus{}multi}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity resolution:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularity has a \sphinxstylestrong{resolution limit}: in undirected graphs it struggles to detect communities much smaller than roughly \(\sqrt{2m}\) (with \(m\) edges). The resolution parameter \(\gamma\) can help:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Modularity vs. resolution:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{γ}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}10}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsh{}Comm}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}10}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Q}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}10}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Avg Size}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZlt{}10}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{45}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{z\PYGZus{}score} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Highly significant (real structure)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{elif} \PYG{n}{z\PYGZus{}score} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Significant (likely real structure)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Interpretation: Not significant (could be random)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Null model comparison:
  Real Q: 0.4589
  Random Q (mean \(\pm\) std): 0.0023 \(\pm\) 0.0145
  Z\PYGZhy{}score: 31.49
  Interpretation: Highly significant (real structure)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Summary of metrics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity (Q):} Overall quality, general\sphinxhyphen{}purpose

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coverage:} Simple interpretability (\% internal edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance:} Balances true positives and true negatives

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Conductance:} Community boundary quality (per\sphinxhyphen{}community)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Null model:} Statistical significance test

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recommendation:} Always report modularity + at least one other metric to get a complete picture.


\subsubsection{CLI Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Reference (Optional)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:cli-cross-reference-optional}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides command\sphinxhyphen{}line tools for quick community detection without writing Python code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic usage:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities using Louvain (default algorithm)}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }louvain\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Using Infomap (requires Infomap binary installed)}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }infomap\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Using Label Propagation (fast for large networks)}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }label\PYGZus{}prop\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With custom resolution parameter for Louvain}
py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }community\PYG{+w}{ }datasets/network.edgelist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}algorithm\PYG{+w}{ }louvain\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}resolution\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}.5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }communities.json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Available algorithms:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain}}: Fast Louvain method (default) \sphinxhyphen{} optimizes modularity on flattened network

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{infomap}}: Infomap algorithm \sphinxhyphen{} requires Infomap binary (\sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{label\_prop}}: Label propagation \sphinxhyphen{} very fast, suitable for large networks

\end{itemize}

For multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific community detection (with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling), use the Python API with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain\_multilayer()}} as shown in the examples above. \subsection{How to Simulate Multilayer Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:how-to-simulate-multilayer-dynamics}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide presents py3plex as a comprehensive framework for simulating dynamical processes on multilayer networks. We cover epidemic models (SIR, SIS), diffusion processes (random walks), and custom dynamics implementations—all with full multilayer support.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{📓 Run this guide online}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can run this tutorial in your browser without any local installation:

\sphinxhref{https://colab.research.google.com/github/SkBlaz/py3plex/blob/master/notebooks/simulate\_dynamics.ipynb}{}
%
\begin{footnote}[7]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://colab.research.google.com/github/SkBlaz/py3plex/blob/master/notebooks/simulate\_dynamics.ipynb}
%
\end{footnote}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Or see the full executable example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sir\_epidemic.py}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A loaded multilayer network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}).


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer dynamics in py3plex enable you to model processes where interactions occur across multiple types of relationships simultaneously. Typical use cases include:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Epidemic spread}: Disease transmission through household, workplace, and social contact layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Information diffusion}: News spreading via online and offline communication channels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random walks}: Navigation and search processes across interconnected network layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Opinion dynamics}: Belief propagation through multiple social contexts

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Simulation Pipeline}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The typical workflow for running dynamics simulations consists of five steps:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Load or build} a multilayer network using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.core.multinet}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose a dynamics model} (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SISDynamics}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RandomWalkDynamics}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Configure parameters} and initial conditions (infection rates, starting nodes, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run the simulation} via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.run(steps=...)}} with a fixed seed for reproducibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inspect the results} object using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.get\_measure(...)}} to extract time series and summary statistics

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pipeline provides a consistent interface across all dynamics models while allowing specialized configurations for multilayer network effects.


\subsubsection{Common Concepts \& API}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:common-concepts-api}}

\paragraph{Node and Layer Representation}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:node-and-layer-representation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dynamics in py3plex operate on the \sphinxstylestrong{supra\sphinxhyphen{}network} representation, where multilayer nodes are encoded as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}} tuples. For example, Alice in the “friends” layer is represented as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}friends\textquotesingle{})}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When you pass a multilayer network to a dynamics model:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node states are tracked per node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Infection, diffusion, or walker movements respect both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can query per\sphinxhyphen{}layer statistics after simulation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For single\sphinxhyphen{}layer NetworkX graphs, nodes are used directly without tuple encoding.


\paragraph{Time and Synchrony}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:time-and-synchrony}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dynamics models in this guide use \sphinxstylestrong{discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time, synchronous updates}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time advances in integer steps: t = 0, 1, 2, …

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
At each step, all nodes update simultaneously based on the state at time t

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This differs from continuous\sphinxhyphen{}time (Gillespie) models, which are also available in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.dynamics}}

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Randomness \& Reproducibility}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:randomness-reproducibility}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every dynamics model has a dedicated random number generator controlled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.set\_seed(seed)}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Setting the seed ensures:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reproducible initial conditions (which nodes start infected, which are susceptible)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reproducible stochastic transitions (infection events, recovery events, random walk steps)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consistent results across multiple runs with the same seed

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Network Requirements}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:network-requirements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dynamics models work with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex multilayer networks}: Full support for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer and intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX graphs}: Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks (directed or undirected)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edge weights}: Epidemic models currently treat edges as unweighted contacts. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RandomWalkDynamics}} samples neighbors uniformly, so weights are ignored unless you implement a weighted variant.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Common Base Interface}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:common-base-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dynamics classes inherit from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsProcess}} (discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ContinuousTimeProcess}} (continuous\sphinxhyphen{}time). The core methods are:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Initialize with network and parameters}
\PYG{n}{dynamics} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set seed for reproducibility}
\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run for specified number of steps}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract measures}
\PYG{n}{prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}counts} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{state\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{results}} object is always a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsResult}} instance with standardized measure extraction methods.
Time series returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.run(steps=k)}} include the initial state at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t=0}}, so arrays have length \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k + 1}}.


\subsubsection{SIR Epidemic Model on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:sir-epidemic-model-on-multilayer-networks}}

\paragraph{Formal Description}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:formal-description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{SIR (Susceptible\sphinxhyphen{}Infected\sphinxhyphen{}Recovered)} model describes epidemic spread with three compartments:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{S (Susceptible)}: Nodes that can become infected

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{I (Infected)}: Nodes that are currently infectious

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{R (Recovered)}: Nodes with permanent immunity (absorbing state)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Discrete\sphinxhyphen{}Time Update Rules} (synchronous):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recovery}: Each infected node recovers (I \(\rightarrow\) R) with probability \(\gamma \in (0, 1)\) per time step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infection}: Each susceptible node with k infected neighbors becomes infected (S \(\rightarrow\) I) with probability
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p_{\text{infect}} = 1 - (1 - \beta)^k\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\beta \in (0, 1)\) is the per\sphinxhyphen{}contact infection probability under independent transmission attempts from each infected neighbor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Absorption}: Recovered nodes remain recovered (R \(\rightarrow\) R) forever

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Extension}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On multilayer networks, the infection pressure on a node aggregates across all layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A susceptible node \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i, layer\_A)}} counts infected neighbors from both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (within \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_A}}) and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (to other layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The built\sphinxhyphen{}in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}} uses a single \(\beta\) value across all layers; to model heterogeneous layers, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:layer-specific-params}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific and Time\sphinxhyphen{}Varying Parameters}}}}} for a small customization pattern

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This means epidemics can spread within layers and jump between layers via inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections, mimicking real\sphinxhyphen{}world scenarios like workplace and household transmission.


\paragraph{Code Example}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:code-example}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{)}

The plot shows the characteristic SIR pattern: S decreases monotonically, I rises then falls (forming a peak), and R increases monotonically until saturation. The peak prevalence and timing depend on β, γ, and network structure.


\subsubsection{SIS Epidemic Model on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:sis-epidemic-model-on-multilayer-networks}}

\paragraph{Formal Description}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{SIS (Susceptible\sphinxhyphen{}Infected\sphinxhyphen{}Susceptible)} model describes epidemics \sphinxstylestrong{without permanent immunity}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{S (Susceptible)}: Nodes that can become infected

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{I (Infected)}: Nodes that are currently infectious

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Discrete\sphinxhyphen{}Time Update Rules} (synchronous):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recovery}: Each infected node recovers (I \(\rightarrow\) S) with probability \(\gamma\) (or \(\mu\)) per time step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infection}: Each susceptible node with k infected neighbors becomes infected (S \(\rightarrow\) I) with probability
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p_{\text{infect}} = 1 - (1 - \beta)^k\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(\beta \in (0, 1)\) is the transmission probability per contact

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No absorption}: Recovered nodes immediately return to susceptible state, allowing reinfection

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Endemic Equilibrium}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike SIR (which eventually dies out), SIS can reach an \sphinxstylestrong{endemic equilibrium} where a steady fraction of nodes remain infected. The basic reproduction number is:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}R_0 = \frac{\beta}{\gamma} \langle k \rangle\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where ⟨k⟩ is the average degree in a homogeneous\sphinxhyphen{}network, small\sphinxhyphen{}\(\beta\) approximation (using \(1 - (1 - \beta)^k \approx \beta k\)). If R\(\sb{\text{0}}\) \textgreater{} 1, endemicity is possible; if R\(\sb{\text{0}}\) ≤ 1, the epidemic dies out in this mean\sphinxhyphen{}field view (heterogeneous networks can shift the threshold).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Extension}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On multilayer networks, SIS infection pressure aggregates across all layers, similar to SIR. The endemic prevalence can differ across layers if you use layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific transmission rates.


\paragraph{Code Example}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id2}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SISDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the same multilayer network as before}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{19}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

                  \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}
                  \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,}
                  \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Infection probability per contact}
    \PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Recovery probability (also accepts \PYGZsq{}gamma\PYGZsq{})}
    \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run for longer to reach equilibrium}
\PYG{n}{sis}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sis}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{200}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract prevalence time series}
\PYG{n}{prevalence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute endemic prevalence (mean of last 50 steps)}

\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Status: Epidemic died out}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected Output}

\paragraph{Comparison with SIR}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:comparison-with-sir}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The key difference between SIS and SIR:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SIR}: Forms a peak and dies out (all nodes eventually become R or remain S)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SIS}: Can sustain long\sphinxhyphen{}term endemic prevalence if R\(\sb{\text{0}}\) \textgreater{} 1

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n+nn}{networkx} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use a denser network to see endemic behavior}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{watts\PYGZus{}strogatz\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{6}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run SIS}
\PYG{n}{sis} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SISDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sis}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sis\PYGZus{}results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sis}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{150}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sis\PYGZus{}prev} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sis\PYGZus{}results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run SIR}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{150}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}prev} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Plot comparison}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{figure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{6}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{xlabel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Time step}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ylabel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Random Walk Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:random-walk-dynamics}}

\paragraph{Formal Description}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id3}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk dynamics simulate the movement of a walker (or multiple walkers) on the network. At each time step:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The walker is at some node (or node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With probability \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lazy\_probability}}, the walker stays at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With probability \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1 \sphinxhyphen{} lazy\_probability}}, the walker moves to a uniformly random neighbor

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Random Walks}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On multilayer networks:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Walkers navigate both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (within a layer) and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges (between layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The state is a node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuple, e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Transition probabilities are uniform over all neighbors (intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer + inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge weights in the graph are ignored in this default implementation; to bias transitions by weight, subclass and resample neighbors proportionally

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walks are fundamental for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computing stationary distributions (related to PageRank and eigenvector centrality)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modeling diffusion and search processes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimating hitting times between nodes

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Code Example}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:id4}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{RandomWalkDynamics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a two\PYGZhy{}layer network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ring structure in layer1, star structure in layer2}
\PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{15}
\PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\paragraph{Analyzing Layer Switching}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:analyzing-layer-switching}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can analyze how often the walker switches between layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count layer switches}
\PYG{n}{switches} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{range}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{current\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{n}{next\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{current\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{!=} \PYG{n}{next\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{switches} \PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Total layer switches: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{switches}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Switch rate: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{switches}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{trajectory}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This reveals how “coupled” the layers are through inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges. High switch rates indicate strong inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connectivity.

\paragraph{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Transmission Rates}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:layer-specific-transmission-rates}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIRDynamics}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SISDynamics}} accept a single scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta}}. To model heterogeneous transmission across layers, subclass the process and choose a layer\sphinxhyphen{}dependent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta}} inside the susceptible transition:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}

\PYG{k}{class} \PYG{n+nc}{LayerAwareSIR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{def} \PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{kwargs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb}{super}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}beta}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{kwargs}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}
        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}rules} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{dict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}rules}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} shallow copy}

        \PYG{k}{def} \PYG{n+nf}{transition\PYGZus{}S}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{isinstance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{tuple}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{k+kc}{None}
            \PYG{n}{beta} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{params}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{beta}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
            \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
            \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
                \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}infect} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{k}
                \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}} \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}infect}\PYG{p}{:}
                    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
            \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}

        \PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}rules}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{transition\PYGZus{}S}

\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}rates} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{household}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{workplace}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{LayerAwareSIR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}betas}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}rates}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After running the simulation, you can compute layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific prevalence manually:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get final state}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count infected nodes per layer}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{isinstance}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{tuple}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer node}
        \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node}
        \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{not} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{S}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{I}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
        \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{state}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Print per\PYGZhy{}layer statistics}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{counts} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}prevalence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{total} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{counts}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layer }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ recovered out of }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{total}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes (}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{counts}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{R}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{total}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Time\sphinxhyphen{}Varying Parameters (Intervention Scenarios)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:time-varying-parameters-intervention-scenarios}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To model interventions (e.g., school closures, social distancing), you can run multiple simulations with different parameters for different time windows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scenario 1: Baseline (no intervention)}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}baseline} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scenario 2: Intervention at t=30 (reduce beta)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run phase 1 (before intervention)}
\PYG{n}{sir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{initial\PYGZus{}infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}30} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{30}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{record}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get state at t=30}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run phase 2 (with reduced beta)}
\PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}intervention} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{SIRDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.15}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}intervention}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Continue from same seed}
\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}intervention} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sir\PYGZus{}intervention}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{70}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{state\PYGZus{}30}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare peak prevalence}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Baseline peak: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}baseline}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Intervention peak: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{results\PYGZus{}intervention}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Note: For more complex time\sphinxhyphen{}varying scenarios, consider using the high\sphinxhyphen{}level simulation builder API (see next steps).}


\subsubsection{Result Objects and Metrics}

\paragraph{DynamicsResult API}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics:dynamicsresult-api}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dynamics models return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DynamicsResult}} object from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.run()}}. This object provides:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Trajectory access}: Direct indexing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{results{[}t{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{results.trajectory}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Measure extraction}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.get\_measure(name)}} for standard metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Conversion}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pandas()}} for DataFrame export

\end{itemize}
