\sphinxstylestrong{Design rationale:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{DSL}: Declarative, optimized for graph queries (layer algebra, centrality, grouping)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pandas}: Procedural, flexible for data transformations (arbitrary computations, reshaping)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Workflow}: Use DSL for graph\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations, export to pandas for data munging

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Example: Combined Workflow}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:example-combined-workflow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A realistic workflow combining both DSL and pandas operations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Scenario: Find influential nodes in social network, normalize scores,}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}           rank within communities, export for visualization}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} DSL: Query and compute graph metrics}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export to pandas for transformations}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pandas: Transform and enhance data}
\PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Normalize centrality to [0, 1]}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{norm\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}betweenness}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}betweenness} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Composite influence score}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{influence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+}
    \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{norm\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+}
    \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Group by community and compute statistics}
\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{groupby}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{agg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{influence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{count}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{max}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{round}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sort communities by average influence}
\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{influence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{ascending}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
              influence
                  count  mean    max
community
5                  23  0.72   0.89
2                  31  0.68   0.85
8                  19  0.61   0.79
1                  28  0.58   0.74
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why this matters:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single pipeline}: No need to export intermediate results to disk or juggle multiple DataFrames

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Flexibility}: DSL for graph operations, pandas for everything else

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance}: DSL computes centrality on the multilayer graph once, pandas transforms in\sphinxhyphen{}memory

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Ecosystem}: Full pandas ecosystem available (plotting, statistics, export formats)

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When to use each:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{DSL alone}: Simple queries, need graph\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations (centrality, grouping, coverage)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pandas alone}: Non\sphinxhyphen{}graph data, pure data transformations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Combined (DSL \(\rightarrow\) pandas)}: Complex analytical workflows, need both graph metrics and custom computations

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Build Analysis Pipelines with Dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style Operations}}}} for the dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style pipeline API (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges()}} functions) which provides an alternative approach using chainable operations directly on networks.

Now that you understand the DSL, explore these related resources:
\begin{itemize}
\item {}

Use it to validate complex queries.

\sphinxstylestrong{Examples Repository} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Examples \& Recipes}}}}): Full scripts showing DSL in context, including data loading, query composition, analysis, and visualization.

\subsection{How to Find Graph Patterns and Motifs with the Pattern Matching API}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:how-to-find-graph-patterns-and-motifs-with-the-pattern-matching-api}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s Pattern Matching Builder API to find graph motifs, paths, triangles, and complex subgraph patterns in multilayer networks.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{🎯 What You’ll Learn}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to express graph patterns using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q.pattern()}} builder API

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to match edges, paths, triangles, and custom motifs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to apply multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}aware constraints (within/between layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to filter patterns using node and edge predicates

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to extract and analyze pattern match results

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{💻 Complete Example}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the full executable example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{example\_pattern\_matching.py}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A loaded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} object (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic familiarity with the DSL (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding of graph motifs (edges, paths, triangles, subgraphs)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Why Pattern Matching?}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:why-pattern-matching}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pattern matching allows you to find \sphinxstylestrong{specific subgraph structures} in your network. Unlike node/edge queries that return individual elements, pattern matching returns \sphinxstylestrong{complete matches} where multiple nodes and edges satisfy structural constraints.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Common Use Cases:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Motif Detection:} Find triangles, cliques, or other structural patterns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Path Analysis:} Discover multi\sphinxhyphen{}hop connections between nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Patterns:} Identify cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer relationships

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complex Queries:} Express “find nodes A, B, C where A connects to B with weight \textgreater{} 0.5, B connects to C, and all are in the social layer”

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comparison to Basic Queries:}


\subsubsection{Quick Start: Your First Pattern}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:quick-start-your-first-pattern}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Let’s start with a simple example: finding all edges in a network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mental model:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q.pattern()}} binds \sphinxstylestrong{variables} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"a"}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"b"}}, etc.) to actual node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuples, then checks that every required edge or path between those variables exists. Each match is a complete mapping of variables \(\rightarrow\) node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuples rather than a single node or edge.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a simple network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
     \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Charlie}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find all edges (simple pattern)}
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}              \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define node variable \PYGZdq{}a\PYGZdq{}}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}              \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define node variable \PYGZdq{}b\PYGZdq{}}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}         \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Require edge between a and b}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ matches}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Found 4 matches
                 a                  b
0  (Alice, social)      (Bob, social)

\subsubsection{Pattern Components}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:pattern-components}}

\paragraph{Nodes}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:nodes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define node variables that will be bound to actual nodes during matching:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Simple node}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node with semantic labels (metadata only)}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{labels}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{person}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node with predicates}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node with layer constraint}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node Predicates:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All standard DSL predicates work with pattern nodes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree\_\_gt=5}} — degree greater than 5

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree\_\_lt=2}} — degree less than 2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer="social"}} — node must be in social layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any node attribute: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{age\_\_gt=30}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type="user"}}, etc.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Edges}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:edges}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define edges between node variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Undirected edge}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edge with predicates}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{weight\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edge with optional type}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{etype}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friendship}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edge Predicates:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter edges by attributes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weight\_\_gt=0.5}} — edge weight greater than 0.5

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weight\_\_lt=1.0}} — edge weight less than 1.0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Any edge attribute: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{timestamp\_\_gt=100}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{color="red"}}, etc.

\paragraph{Paths}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:paths}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sugar method for defining sequential connections:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2\PYGZhy{}hop path: a \(\rightarrow\) b \(\rightarrow\) c}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Equivalent to:}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Directed path}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Paths enforce adjacency in the order you list the variables; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directed=True}} the edges must follow that direction.

\subsubsection{Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}Aware Patterns}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:multilayer-aware-patterns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
One of the most powerful features is specifying layer constraints on edges.


\paragraph{Within Layer}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:within-layer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find edges that exist within a single layer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edges within the social layer}
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Between Layers}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:between-layers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find edges that cross between specific layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edges between social and work layers}
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{between\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Any Layer}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:any-layer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow edges in any layer (default behavior; call it explicitly if you want the query to read clearly):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{Example 1: Find Triangles with Weight Constraints}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:example-1-find-triangles-with-weight-constraints}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Find triangles where all edges have weight \textgreater{} 1.0.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{weight\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{weight\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{weight\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{triangles} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{triangles}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ triangles}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you prefer the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{triangle()}} sugar, expand it as above to attach edge predicates, or apply the weight filter after executing the simpler triangle pattern.

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{weight\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ensure different nodes}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ high\PYGZhy{}degree pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Unique nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Working with Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:working-with-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PatternQueryResult}} object provides multiple ways to access matches. Use raw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rows}} for programmatic iteration, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_pandas}} for tabular analysis, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_nodes}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_edges}} when you want to pass results back into graph algorithms.


\paragraph{Accessing Rows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:accessing-rows}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all matches as list of dictionaries}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{match} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{rows}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Match: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{match}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} e.g., \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}a\PYGZsq{}: (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}), \PYGZsq{}b\PYGZsq{}: (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{})\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result.count}} is the number of rows returned, equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{len(result.rows)}}.
Each row maps your variable names to concrete \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node, layer)}} tuples.


\paragraph{Converting to Pandas}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:converting-to-pandas}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now use pandas operations}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export to CSV}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pattern\PYGZus{}matches.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Column order follows the variables you specified with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.returning(...)}}; if you did not set it, all variables are returned in declaration order.


\paragraph{Extracting Nodes}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:extracting-nodes}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all matched nodes (as tuples)}
\PYG{n}{all\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get unique nodes only}
\PYG{n}{unique\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes for specific variables}
\PYG{n}{a\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{vars}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Extracting Edges}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:extracting-edges}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all matched edges as tuples}
\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Each edge is a (source\PYGZus{}tuple, target\PYGZus{}tuple) pair}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{src}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dst} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Edge: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{src}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{dst}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Creating Subgraphs}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:creating-subgraphs}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create induced subgraph of matched nodes}
\PYG{n}{subgraph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now use NetworkX operations}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subgraph has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subgraph has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create one subgraph per match}
\PYG{n}{subgraphs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{per\PYGZus{}match}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Created }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{subgraphs}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ subgraphs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Filtering Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:filtering-results}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Filter matches using a predicate}
\PYG{n}{filtered} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{match}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{match}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{startswith}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{A}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Limit number of results}
\PYG{n}{limited} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} return new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PatternQueryResult}} objects; they do not modify the original result.


\subsubsection{Query Execution Planning}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:query-execution-planning}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain()}} to see how the pattern will be executed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{plan} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Root variable: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{root\PYGZus{}var}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Join order: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{var}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{for}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o+ow}{in}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{join\PYGZus{}order}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Estimated complexity: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{estimated\PYGZus{}complexity}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Root variable: a
Join order: [\PYGZsq{}a\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}b\PYGZsq{}]
Estimated complexity: 1000
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The planner chooses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}} as the root because it has the most restrictive predicates (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree\_\_gt=3}}), which will generate fewer candidates.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimated\_complexity}} field is a relative heuristic, useful for comparing different patterns rather than predicting exact runtime.


\subsubsection{Performance Tips}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:performance-tips}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Add Predicates Early:} The more selective predicates you add to the root variable, the faster the query.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Restrictive predicate on first node}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Less efficient: No predicates}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Layer Constraints:} Layer filters significantly reduce the search space.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Restrict to one layer}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Less efficient: Search all layers}
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Set Limits:} For large networks, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.limit()}} to cap results.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Constraints:} Add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a != b}} constraints to avoid self\sphinxhyphen{}loops if not needed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Return only needed variables:} Reducing the result width lowers serialization overhead.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Advanced Features}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:advanced-features}}

\paragraph{Constraints}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:constraints}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Global constraints that apply across variables:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} All\PYGZhy{}different constraint}
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b != c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{constraint}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a != c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Returning Specific Variables}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:returning-specific-variables}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, all variables are returned. You can select specific ones:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pattern} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{b}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{returning}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{a}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{c}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Only return endpoints}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Result only contains \PYGZsq{}a\PYGZsq{} and \PYGZsq{}c\PYGZsq{} columns}

\paragraph{Execution Options}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set maximum matches}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}matches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}

\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:pattern-matching-vs-dsl-node-edge-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use node/edge queries when you need individual elements. Use pattern matching when you need to find subgraph structures.


\subsubsection{Limitations and Future Work}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:limitations-and-future-work}}

\paragraph{Current Limitations (v1)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:current-limitations-v1}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fixed\sphinxhyphen{}length paths only:} Variable\sphinxhyphen{}length paths like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(a)\sphinxhyphen{}{[}*1..3{]}\sphinxhyphen{}(b)}} not yet supported

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No optional matching:} All pattern elements must match

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No UNION patterns:} Cannot express “match pattern A OR pattern B”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Limited aggregation:} Aggregation over matches not yet implemented

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These features are planned for future versions while maintaining the current clean API.


\paragraph{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Start simple:} Begin with small patterns and add complexity incrementally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Test on small data:} Validate pattern logic on toy networks before scaling up

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use explain():} Check execution plans for complex queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Combine with DSL:} Use pattern matching for structure, DSL for attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Document patterns:} Add comments explaining complex pattern logic

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:troubleshooting}}

\paragraph{Pattern Returns No Matches}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:pattern-returns-no-matches}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Your pattern should match but returns 0 results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check layer constraints — are nodes actually in the layers you specified?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify predicates — are the thresholds too restrictive?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain()}} to see the execution plan

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test with simpler patterns first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check if your network has the expected structure

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Debug: Check basic statistics first}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Social layer has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{intralayer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Network has }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ intralayer edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Too Many Matches}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:too-many-matches}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Pattern returns too many results.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add more predicates to narrow the search

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.limit()}} to cap results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add layer constraints to restrict search space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.constraint("a != b")}} to avoid duplicates

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Limit results}
\PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Slow Performance}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_patterns:slow-performance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Pattern matching takes too long.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solutions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add selective predicates to the root variable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use layer constraints to reduce search space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider breaking pattern into smaller sub\sphinxhyphen{}patterns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.explain()}} to check estimated complexity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set timeout to avoid runaway queries

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set timeout}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pattern}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{timeout}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{30.0}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{How to Build Analysis Pipelines with Dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:how-to-build-analysis-pipelines-with-dplyr-style-operations}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Chain operations to build reproducible analysis workflows on node or edge tables.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} Load a network first (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes(...)}} returns a chainable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NodeFrame}} (view over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}}, etc.); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges(...)}} returns an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EdgeFrame}}. Examples below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NodeFrame}} and end with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pandas()}} to materialize results.


\subsubsection{Quickstart}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:quickstart}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter \(\rightarrow\) add a column \(\rightarrow\) sort \(\rightarrow\) convert to pandas:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build pipeline: filter \(\rightarrow\) add a column \(\rightarrow\) sort \(\rightarrow\) convert to pandas}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{score}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Available Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:available-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Common verbs you can chain on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes(...)}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges(...)}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}}: keep rows that satisfy a predicate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mutate}}: add or modify columns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select}}: choose columns (and optionally reorder)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arrange}}: sort by a column or key function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}} + \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarise}}: aggregate per group

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}: keep the first \sphinxstyleemphasis{n} rows (useful for previews)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{filter()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:filter}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select rows based on conditions. Chain multiple filters for readability:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{mutate()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:mutate}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add or modify columns using callables that receive each row (a dict\sphinxhyphen{}like object):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}squared}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}hub}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{select()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:select}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose specific columns (and optionally reorder them):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{select}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{arrange()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:arrange}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sort results (ascending by default, or descending with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reverse=True}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Descending}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{group\_by() and summarise()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:group-by-and-summarise}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate by one or more columns. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarise}} expects functions that return scalars (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{len}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summarise}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{count}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Illustrative output (values depend on your data):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
      layer  avg\PYGZus{}degree  max\PYGZus{}degree  count
0   friends        3.45          12     46
1      work        2.87           8     46
2    family        4.12          15     42
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Complex Pipelines}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:complex-pipelines}}

\paragraph{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Step Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:multi-step-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine several verbs to narrow down to the most active nodes. This example assumes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}} columns already exist (e.g., after computing node statistics):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 1: Filter active nodes}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 2: Add computed score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 3: Filter by score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 4: Sort by score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 5: Get top 20}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to pandas}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Combining with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:combining-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mix dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style operations with DSL queries to narrow down candidates, then enrich them:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the same network as above}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use DSL to select nodes and compute measures once}

\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{selected} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{computed}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use dplyr\PYGZhy{}style to filter and transform the same nodes}
\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}

        \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{betweenness}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100}

\subsubsection{Scikit\sphinxhyphen{}learn\sphinxhyphen{}style Pipelines}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:scikit-learn-style-pipelines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pipeline}} to chain reusable steps (each step implements \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform}} and receives the previous output). The first step should handle \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{None}} input (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LoadStep}} does). Replace or extend steps with your own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PipelineStep}} subclasses when needed.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pipeline} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Pipeline}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LoadStep}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{FilterNodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ComputeStats}

\PYG{n}{pipe} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Pipeline}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{load}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{LoadStep}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{filter}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{FilterNodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{stats}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ComputeStats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{include\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pipe}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{stats}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom steps can wrap scikit\sphinxhyphen{}learn components if they implement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transform}} (and optionally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fit}}) to accept the previous step’s output and return the next input.

    \PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\subsubsection{DSL\sphinxhyphen{}Driven Analysis Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/reproduce_workflows:dsl-driven-analysis-workflows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s DSL to create reproducible, declarative analysis pipelines.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL expresses analysis workflows as queries rather than imperative code, keeping them readable and reproducible. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}} builds a query, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} is a layer helper, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query}} returns dictionaries keyed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer)}} tuples.


\paragraph{Basic DSL Workflow Pattern}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/reproduce_workflows:basic-dsl-workflow-pattern}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Template for DSL\sphinxhyphen{}first analysis:} Keep the pipeline linear—load, query, refine, export—so each step can be repeated with different parameters.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from} \PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl} \PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{py3plex/datasets/\PYGZus{}data/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2. Query and filter nodes with DSL}
\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} dict keyed by (node\PYGZus{}id, layer) \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} metrics}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 3. Extract subnetwork}
\PYG{n}{subgraph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 4. Analyze subnetwork}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{High\PYGZhy{}degree subnetwork:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Edges: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 5. Export results}
\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n+nn}{pandas} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n+nn}{pd}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{node}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}analysis.csv}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstylestrong{Notes:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query}} returns a dictionary; access community members via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result{[}"nodes"{]}}} as shown. Community labels live on the NetworkX backing graph (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network.core\_network}}), so they persist across subsequent DSL queries.

\subsection{Multilayer Networks 101}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:multilayer-networks-101}}\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter explains what multilayer networks are, when to use them, and how to choose the right type for your data—without flattening away important structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{You will learn:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
What distinguishes multilayer from single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Types: multiplex, heterogeneous, temporal, interdependent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When to use multilayer modeling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Common pitfalls to avoid

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Key ideas to keep in mind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{layer} labels the context of an interaction (relationship type, time slice, modality).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} is the atomic unit; the same node can appear in multiple layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coupling} uses inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges that link the same entity across layers, with a weight controlling how strongly layers influence each other. When the weight is 0, layers are independent; higher weights make layers behave more coherently.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{What are Multilayer Networks?}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:what-are-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer network} models systems with multiple types of relationships, node types, or interaction contexts while keeping each interaction labeled by its layer. Each edge carries both endpoints \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} the layer context, so interactions remain distinguishable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:} A researcher’s social world includes coauthors, colleagues, students, and Twitter followers. These are different relationship types with different meanings. A multilayer network keeps them as separate \sphinxstylestrong{layers} rather than flattening into one graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Traditional vs. Multilayer:}
